_comment: Combinations ZUZZ may not synthesise, split by how they are treated.
always_blocked  - refused outright at every trust level. Ctrl+Alt+Del and
Ctrl+Shift+Esc are the secure-attention and task-manager
sequences; an agent that reaches for them is trying to get
past a boundary the user can see.
requires_confirmation - allowed only after an explicit answer, and the
confirmation text says what will happen. Win+L locks the
machine with no warning, Win+R opens a run box that executes
anything, and Alt+F4 closes whatever has focus.
Modifiers are compared in any order, so ('ctrl','alt','delete') and
('alt','ctrl','delete') are the same combination. Adding a combination here
is the only way to block one: there is no inline exemption.
_reserved_comment: Ctrl+Shift+Q is ZUZZ's own emergency stop, handled by a separate process.
ZUZZ never synthesises it: doing so would stop itself by accident, and the
stop must always be something the human presses, never something the agent
types. It is refused at every trust level.
